pages.text: $(#555)$(o)(3D scene not available in this version)$()$(br2)Spatial IO is a way to cut-and-paste physical volumes of space in your world. It can be used to move $(l:items_blocks_machines/budding_certus)Flawless Budding Certus Quartz$(/l), have a room in your base where you can swap out various interiors to use it for different purposes, or even move the end portal!

It works by $(o)swapping$() the defined volume with an identically-sized volume in the spatial storage dimension, sending whatever's in the pylon array to the spatial storage dimension, and whatever's in the dimension to the pylon array.$(br2)This means that if you have a way of travelling between dimensions (spatial IO $(o)can$() be used to make a teleporter, but doing it is very complex, a bit janky, and beyond the scope of
the guide), you can use them like custom-sized compact machines or pocket dimensions.

pages.title: The Multiblock Setup
pages.text: Spatial IO requires a specific arrangement of its components in order to function, and define the volume to be cut-and-pasted.$(br2)All of the components must be on the same $(l:ae2_mechanics/me_network_connections)network$(/l) in order to function, and you can have only one spatial IO setup on a network. Thus, a $(l:ae2_mechanics/subnetworks)subnetwork$(/l) is recommended.

The $(l:items_blocks_machines/spatial_io_port)Spatial IO Port$(/l) controls the spatial IO operation. It shows stats on the multiblock setup, and holds the $(l:items_blocks_machines/spatial_cells)spatial cells$(/l)$(br2)It shows$(li)Stored and max $(l:ae2_mechanics/energy)energy$(/l) in the network$(li)Required energy to perform the operation. This can be quite large and is used

instantaneously, so make sure you have enough $(l:items_blocks_machines/energy_cells)energy cells$(/l) to hold it all.$(li)Efficiency of the pylon array$(li)Size of the defined volume$(br2)To perform a spatial IO operation, place a spatial storage cell in the input slot and give the spatial IO port a redstone pulse. It will then $(o)swap$() the volume in the pylons with the volume in the spatial storage dimension. This means that if you send some set of

blocks to the spatial storage dimension, $(o)then put another set of blocks in the pylons$(), put the cell back in the input slot, and trigger the IO port again, the 2nd set of blocks will disappear and the 1st set of blcks will reappear.$(br2)$(bold)BE CAREFUL, Any entity in the defined volume, including you, will be carried along, and if you have no way of getting out, you will be trapped in the spatial storage$()
$(bold)dimension, in a dark, featureless box.$() Use this to prank your friends!

$(l:items_blocks_machines/spatial_pylon)Spatial Pylon$(/l)s are the main part of a spatial IO setup, and define the volume to be affected.$(br2)The volume is defined by the bounding box of the outside of the pylons, contracted in by 1 block in all directions.$(br2)The rules are:$(li)Minimum size of 3x3x3 (which

defines a 1x1x1 volume)$(li)All spatial pylons must be in the outside bounding box$(li)All spatial pylons must be on the same network$(li)All pylons must be at least 2 blocks long$(br2)For example, say you want to define a 3x3x3 volume. Following rule 2, all of the pylons must be within a 5x5x5 shell around the volume you want to define. They can be in almost any configuration, as long as they're contained
within that 1-block-thick 5x5x5 shell.$(br2)$(#555)$(o)(3D scene not available in this version)$()$(br2)A more reasonable setup is this:$(br2)$(#555)$(o)(3D scene not available in this version)$()

pages.title: Efficiency
pages.text: The efficiency of the pylon array depends on the amount of the shell that you fill. Minimal setups around large volumes will be very inefficient and possibly require $(o)billions$() of AE.

pages.title: Cell Dimensions
pages.text: Once a $(l:items_blocks_machines/spatial_cells)spatial cell$(/l) has been used, it gains a permanently defined set of XYZ dimensions (eg, 3x4x2) and is linked to a volume of space in the spatial storage dimension. $(bold)YOU CANNOT RESET, REFORMAT, OR RESIZE A SPATIAL CELL AFTER IT HAS BEEN USED.$() Make a new cell if you want to use different dimensions.$(br2)These are not the same dimensions in the name of a cell, a 16^3 cell can have any

dimensions $(o)up to$() 16x16x16$(br2)Note that this volume is directional and cannot be rotated. A 2x2x3 volume is not the same as a 3x2x2 volume, even though they're the same size.$(br2)if the XYZ dimensions of a cell do not match the defined volume (seen in the IO port), the IO port will not operate.
